quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle, what should a small vehicle driver be ready for?

options.text: Loud noises.
Excess air pollution.
Wind gusts from the large vehicle.
Falling vehicle parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create wind gusts strong enough to push smaller vehicles sideways. Small vehicle drivers should be ready to steer carefully when passing large vehicles traveling at high speeds.

questions.question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?

options.text: Turn on your car radio.
Slow down.
Stop regularly to rest.
Move your eyes side to side as you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop regularly to rest.
questions.explanation: Plan regular stops on long trips. Take time to rest and stretch, even if you don't feel tired.

questions.question: What should you do when merging into a crowded freeway?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Use the entrance ramp to match freeway speed.
Yield to traffic already on the freeway.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to reach freeway speed and yield to existing traffic. Before merging, check your mirrors and blind spots to make sure it is safe to enter.

questions.question: What is the 'No zone'?

options.text: Blind spots around trucks and buses.
A special speed zone.
A road with restrictions on stereo volume.
A television show.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blind spots around trucks and buses.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on both sides, in the back, and in the front. Cars in these areas cannot be seen. These are called 'No zones.'

questions.question: At an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?

options.text: You don't need to stop.
Just slow down to check for crossing traffic.
Stop where you can see 200 feet in both directions, even if you enter the intersecting road.
Stop where you can see approaching traffic before entering the intersecting road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can see approaching traffic before entering the intersecting road.
questions.explanation: Stop at the point closest to the intersecting road where you can see oncoming traffic. Do not enter the intersecting road to get a better view.

questions.question: You see a railroad crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Approach with extreme caution and cross only when sure no train is coming.
Turn down your radio to listen for an approaching train.
Wait for a flagger's signal if one is present.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, follow their instructions.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the pavement mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is not allowed.
Passing is allowed at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during daylight only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines show that traffic is moving in opposite directions. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: How does increasing your speed affect your vision?

options.text: It increases your field of vision.
It decreases your field of vision.
It makes it easier to see cross traffic.
It has no effect on your field of vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: It decreases your field of vision.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the narrower your field of vision becomes. As speed increases, you must watch more carefully for hazards.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you feel tired.
Always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes or passing. Only stop on the shoulder in emergencies. Change lanes as little as possible. Don't use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, when should you proceed?

options.text: Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go when the train passes.
Go when one track is free.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, don't move as soon as a train passes. Wait until you can see all tracks clearly. Even with one track, check again for another approaching train before crossing.

questions.question: When should you use your high beam headlights?

options.text: When driving in dark areas where you cannot see the road ahead.
In heavy fog.
When approaching a vehicle in front of you.
When approaching traffic from the opposite direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving in dark areas where you cannot see the road ahead.
questions.explanation: High beams let you see about 350 feet ahead. Use them in dark areas when you cannot see the road surface ahead. Switch to low beams when you are within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle or within 200 feet of a vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn off all your lights.
Use your parking lights only.
Use your headlights only.
Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams on.
questions.explanation: When you stop on the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beam headlights on. This makes sure other drivers can clearly see your vehicle.

questions.question: You notice a vehicle defect that may affect safe operation. What should you do?

options.text: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
Fix the defect when you have money.
Drive at slower speeds.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any defect that may affect safe operation must be fixed as soon as possible. Fix defects before you drive the vehicle.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.

options.text: Increase
Maintain
Vary
Reduce

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed when turning. This lets you keep control of your vehicle, stay in your lane, and react to surprises.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle that just parked on the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Assume the driver will open the door as you approach.
Speed up.
Slam on your brakes.
Assume the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the driver will open the door as you approach.
questions.explanation: When passing a parked vehicle, assume the driver will open the door as you approach. Be very careful when driving near parked vehicles.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic signal requires the same action as:

options.text: A slow sign.
A yield sign.
A stop sign.
An intersection sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red signal means you must stop. Yield to all traffic that does not have to stop.

questions.question: Distracted drivers have a higher crash risk when using which of these?

options.text: CD player
Radio
Cell phone
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone, radio, or CD player while driving is dangerous and increases crash risk. Even hands-free phones can distract you from the road.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Watch for drunk drivers.
Dangerous curve ahead.
Bump in the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow. They warn you of hazards ahead. This sign warns that wet pavement is slippery and makes vehicles hard to control.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: One-way traffic.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic.
Keep left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow. They warn of hazards ahead. This sign warns that a divided highway is coming.

questions.question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, what happens?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate.
One driver should go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: Vehicles at a four-way stop should go in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are crossing illegally.
Give the right-of-way only when the pedestrian has the legal right to cross.
Slow down and honk your horn near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are crossing illegally.
questions.explanation: You must do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle, no matter what. Drivers must always watch for pedestrians and give them the right-of-way, even if they are crossing where they should not.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Communicate with other drivers and road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other drivers and road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or change direction. Use your lights and horn when needed.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area of the road:

options.text: You cannot see without turning your head.
Directly behind your vehicle.
You can see in your rearview mirror.
You can see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are located to the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: If you need to drive in foggy weather:

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
It is okay to drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: You must use your headlights when visibility is 500 feet or less. Use low beams in fog. High beams reflect light back into your eyes and make it harder to see.

questions.question: You should be cautious when passing a bicycle because:

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.
The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing a bicycle because the cyclist may need to swerve suddenly to avoid an object on the road. Always drive carefully near cyclists.
